title: automation: tenant RBAC bootstrap for Private installer (Helm + Terraform)
author: Elena Park
description: Add automated tenant RBAC bootstrap for Redwood Private installer with Helm and Terraform integrations. Motivation: private deployments need a reproducible, minimal-privilege bootstrap path for tenant onboarding that works across the Helm chart installer and Terraform provisioning flow. This PR implements: 1) declarative tenant role + rolebinding manifests that are templated for the Helm chart; 2) a Terraform module that creates the tenant bootstrap service account, applies required ClusterRoleBindings, and exposes an idempotent apply operation; 3) a CLI-driven automation hook in the private-installer chart that can be run during post-install to initialize tenant identities; 4) improved RBAC test coverage and e2e smoke tests for installer flows. The description below contains the design, testing, and rollout plan. Design: tenant bootstrap uses a minimal set of roles: tenant-admin, tenant-reader, tenant-operator. Roles are scoped to the tenant namespace when possible; cluster-level permissions are limited to controller bootstrapping (CRD initializers, CR creation for tenant-scoped resources). The Terraform module mirrors the same role templates and exposes variables for tenant_name, namespace, and existing_service_account. For Helm the templates live under charts/private-installer/templates/rbac and include integration with chart hooks (post-install, post-upgrade). Rollout: feature gated behind helm value rbac.bootstrap.enabled=false by default; Terraform module must be opted in. Backwards compatibility: installer still supports manual RBAC application; this automation path is additive. Checklist: - [x] role manifests added - [x] helm templates + hooks - [x] terraform module + tests - [x] unit tests for rbac generator - [x] e2e smoke in perf-canary private flow - [x] docs and migration notes Testing: unit tests for template rendering, CI lint and chart-test, terraform fmt/validate + terratest-like smoke. Observability: metrics events emitted during bootstrap (rbac.bootstrap.attempt, rbac.bootstrap.success, rbac.bootstrap.failure) to help debug. Security review: scoped and audited by security team (see linked Linear items).

diff_snippets:
--- charts/private-installer/templates/rbac/tenant-roles.yaml +++
+apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
+kind: Role
+metadata:
+  name: {{ include "private-installer.fullname" . }}-tenant-admin
+  namespace: {{ .Values.tenant.namespace }}
+rules:
+  - apiGroups: [""]
+    resources: ["pods", "services"]
+    verbs: ["get", "list", "watch", "create", "delete"]

--- charts/private-installer/templates/hooks/post-install-bootstrap.yaml +++
+apiVersion: batch/v1
+kind: Job
+metadata:
+  name: private-installer-rbac-bootstrap-{{ .Release.Name }}
+  annotations:
+    helm.sh/hook: post-install,post-upgrade
+spec: ...
release_notes: Adds automated tenant RBAC bootstrap for Private installer (Helm + Terraform). Optional feature behind chart value rbac.bootstrap.enabled. Includes terraform module, helm hooks, tests, and docs.
upgrade_notes: Enabled via --set rbac.bootstrap.enabled=true for Helm installs or by calling the terraform module. Existing manual RBAC applies continue to work. See docs/private-installer/rbac-bootstrap.md for migration steps.
observability_notes: Bootstrap emits metrics rbac.bootstrap.attempt/success/failure and logs events to kube-events namespace. CI included a smoke that verifies metric emission.
security_audit: Security review completed: reduced cluster scope, added audit annotations, and explicit allow-list for controller actions. See SEC-119 linked linear ticket.
notes_for_ops: When upgrading older installations, run helm upgrade with rbac.bootstrap.enabled=false initially to validate, then toggle true to run bootstrap. Terraform users must set create_sa=true to enable automatic SA creation.
example_usage: Helm: helm install redwood ./charts/private-installer --set rbac.bootstrap.enabled=true --set tenant.name=acme
